title: Rate-limited config propagation caused staggered promotion drift during canary swap
creator: Priya Desai
description: During a routine canary promotion for model v2026-02B we observed a multi-minute divergence between control-plane intent and data-plane traffic split. A subset of route voters continued sending traffic to the old variant leading to a visible increase in 5xx rates and request latency for ~7% of requests for ~12 minutes. This ticket captures the postmortem, short-term mitigations applied, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-08 11:12 UTC: Canary promotion requested by CD pipeline.
2026-02-08 11:13 UTC: Control plane accepted promotion intent and persisted deployment metadata.
2026-02-08 11:13:30 UTC: Orchestrator nodes begin applying config; approx 30% of nodes report updated route table within 20s.
2026-02-08 11:14 UTC: SRE pager triggers - spike in 5xx and tail latency on canary route observed by dashboard.
2026-02-08 11:17 UTC: Root cause suspected: config-propagation lag. Investigation started.
2026-02-08 11:20 UTC: Temporary roll-forward aborted; attempted rollback failed due to stale version-pin state on several orchestrators.
2026-02-08 11:24 UTC: We disabled per-tenant propagation rate limiter for the affected shard and retried propagation. Convergence achieved by 11:25 UTC.
2026-02-08 11:30 UTC: Incident declared mitigated. Post-incident monitoring continued for 2h.
impact: Approximately 7% of global requests to the affected route experienced elevated error rates (5xx) and 200-300ms additional latency during the window. No customer data loss. Several high-volume customers reported transient errors; one customer reported SLA impact and filed a support ticket.
root_cause: The config fanout service introduced a per-tenant rate-limiter to protect downstream orchestrators during high churn. The limiter used a token-bucket with a conservative refill tuned for steady-state churn. During this promotion, the limiter interacted badly with our staged fanout strategy: some orchestrator shards received metadata early while others were delayed. The delayed shards held older version pins, which prevented the rollback path from cleanly unpinning and caused a transient mixed-serve state. Additionally, our rollout gating lacked a convergence check (we only checked acceptance, not full handshake completion).
mitigation:
Short-term: Removed the per-tenant refill cap for the affected shard and forced a synchronous propagation to all orchestrators for the in-flight promotion. Added a temporary monitor to alert on per-route propagation skew >30s.
Mid-term: Added an automated retry path that detects stale version pins and triggers a safe rollforward or coordinated unpin; improved rollback idempotency.
Long-term: Replace the global per-tenant limiter with a backpressure-aware fanout that respects per-orchestrator health and queue depth, and introduce a 'promotion convergence' SLO that blocks final canary completion until all orchestrators report handshake success.
